  "text": "The boy went upstairs. They heard him stop on the landing, then go on.

“My wife's up there,” he said.

“I know.”

“She isn't well.”

The woman kept her foot against the door. Her shoe had split beside the little toe. He looked at that rather than at the handle, which was moving slowly enough that he could almost persuade himself it wasn't moving at all.

“Is this about the prescription?”

“No.”

“Because I collected it.”

“You did.”

The boy came down holding a pillowcase by its gathered neck. Something inside knocked against his knee at each step.

“Not those,” the woman said.

“He said everything loose.”

For the first time, she looked uncertain.

“Who said?” he asked.

The boy put the pillowcase beside the money. A corner of it fell open. He saw his wife's hairbrush, the bedside clock, a white cup with a brown line inside it. Last came her wedding ring, rolling briefly before it settled against the clock.

He picked it up. There was soap caught beneath the setting.

“She doesn't take this off.”

From upstairs came the sound of a drawer closing.

The woman lifted her foot from the cupboard.

“Then you'd better give it back.”

He went to the stairs with the ring held tightly between finger and thumb. On the third step he stopped.

Behind him, the cupboard opened. No one spoke. He heard the boy gathering the coins from the table, one at a time.

“Anne?” he called.

The bedside clock began to ring downstairs.

His wife answered from the cupboard.

“Don't come up yet.”"
